framework_name: B.C. Government Public Sector Investment Prioritization Framework

categories.name: Drivers
categories.description: Urgency and necessity driven by legislation, mandated government commitments, forced technology end-of-life, or acute operational risk.

rubric.1-3: Low urgency: discretionary improvement with no legal, compliance, or critical risk driver.
rubric.4-6: Moderate urgency: addresses known operational friction, outdated workflow, or anticipated policy direction.
rubric.7-8: High urgency: direct ministry priority, significant operational risk, or impending technology deprecation.
rubric.9-10: Critical / Mandatory: explicit legislative mandate, court order, immediate security vulnerability, or system failure risk.

categories.name: Strategic Alignment
categories.description: Alignment with provincial government priorities, ministry service plan goals, and branch strategic objectives.

rubric.1-3: Weak alignment: isolated team benefit with minimal connection to broader ministry or sector goals.
rubric.4-6: Indirect alignment: supports general organizational efficiency or secondary service plan goals.
rubric.7-8: Strong alignment: directly reinforces primary ministry strategic objectives or branch commitments.
rubric.9-10: Transformational alignment: core pillar of provincial government priorities (e.g., Access to Justice, DRIPA, modern services).

categories.name: Outcomes and Benefits
categories.description: Magnitude and breadth of measurable public, citizen, operational, and financial outcomes (e.g., cycle time reduction, user satisfaction).

rubric.1-3: Minor benefit: localized cosmetic improvement or marginal time savings for a small group.
rubric.4-6: Noticeable benefit: measurable efficiency gains, error reductions, or workflow speedup for branch staff.
rubric.7-8: Substantial benefit: major public access improvement, significant cost avoidance, or systemic process enhancement.
rubric.9-10: Profound benefit: sector-wide transformation, hundreds of hours saved, dramatic public accessibility and equity enhancement.

categories.name: Sector Benefits & Reusability
categories.description: Contribution to cross-agency collaboration, shared digital infrastructure, reusable components, or sector-wide standards.

rubric.1-3: Siloed: single bespoke tool with zero reuse potential across other branches or ministries.
rubric.4-6: Limited reuse: patterns or components could inform adjacent projects with moderate refactoring.
rubric.7-8: High reuse: directly usable API, shared data service, or common business capability across justice partners.
rubric.9-10: Foundational sector platform: standard enterprise capability adopted across the justice and public safety sector.

categories.name: Organizational Readiness & Capacity
categories.description: Team capacity, change management readiness, and organizational bandwidth to absorb and adopt the change.

rubric.1-3: Low readiness: team severely constrained, acute change fatigue, no dedicated personnel available.
rubric.4-6: Moderate readiness: team can absorb change with external support or backfill arrangements.
rubric.7-8: High readiness: core team identified, management support strong, change network established.
rubric.9-10: Exceptional readiness: dedicated multidisciplinary team assembled, change champion network active, full capacity committed.

categories.name: Extent of Research & Discovery
categories.description: Depth of problem validation, user research, service design, technical feasibility, and cross-jurisdictional evidence.

rubric.1-3: Unvalidated idea: conceptual request based on assumptions with no formal discovery or user research.
rubric.4-6: Preliminary research: problem statement defined, baseline desk research completed, informal user feedback gathered.
rubric.7-8: Validated discovery: thorough service design, user journeys mapped, cross-jurisdictional review, technical spikes run.
rubric.9-10: De-risked prototype: tested clickable prototype or pilot with live users, clear quantitative evidence, validated architecture.

categories.name: Investment Cost & Affordability
categories.description: Financial feasibility, capital/operating funding requirements, resource expenditure, and cost certainty (higher score = lower cost/greater affordability).

rubric.1-3: High cost / Unfunded: massive multi-million capital requirement, high ongoing licensing, unbudgeted.
rubric.4-6: Substantial cost: significant funding required, within reach of grant or capital request but requires trade-offs.
rubric.7-8: Manageable cost: modest capital/operating cost easily covered within existing branch budget or minor allocation.
rubric.9-10: Low cost / Highly affordable: minimal or zero new capital needed, leverages existing in-house tools and licenses.

categories.name: Executive Sponsorship & Support
categories.description: Strength and seniority of sponsorship, stakeholder coalition, and governance backing.

rubric.1-3: No confirmed sponsor: grassroots proposal without branch director or executive advocacy.
rubric.4-6: Supportive leadership: senior manager or director endorses the direction but has not committed capital.
rubric.7-8: Committed executive sponsor: Assistant Deputy Minister or Executive Director actively champions the initiative.
rubric.9-10: Unified governance coalition: joint sponsorship across Court Services Branch, Judiciary, and Ministry executive.

categories.name: Ease of Implementation & Low Complexity
categories.description: Implementation simplicity, low technical and privacy debt, few vendor dependencies, and straightforward governance (higher score = easier implementation).

rubric.1-3: Extremely complex: multi-system integration, high privacy/security constraints, complex judicial independence rules.
rubric.4-6: Moderate complexity: requires coordination across 2-3 systems and basic privacy impact assessments.
rubric.7-8: Straightforward: standard modern architecture, well-understood patterns, minor third-party dependencies.
rubric.9-10: Turnkey / Low friction: self-contained delivery, zero legacy friction, rapid time-to-value.

definitions.name: Strategic Priorities & Quick Wins
definitions.action: Fund and execute immediately. High public value with high confidence of successful delivery.

definitions.name: Strategic Big Bets
definitions.action: De-risk before full funding. Commission discovery, feasibility studies, service design, or capacity building.

definitions.name: Tactical Efficiencies
definitions.action: Deliver opportunistically if excess capacity exists, or bundle into broader modernization packages.

definitions.name: Deprioritize & Defer
definitions.action: Defer, re-scope, or decline funding. Low public value combined with high delivery friction.
